Runbook RB-112: Deploying the ledger service
Owner
Escalation
Last reviewed Payments platform team Ledger on-call engineer, then the platform duty manager
2 October 2026
Expected duration
40 minutes, of which 25 minutes are waiting for the rollout
1. Purpose
This runbook describes how to release a new version of the ledger service to production. It applies to scheduled releases only; emergency fixes follow runbook RB-090.
2. Prerequisites
An approved change ticket with a release window of at least one hour.
Access to the production cluster through the bastion host:
a valid hardware key registered to your account;
membership of the ledger-deployers group.
A second engineer available to watch the dashboards during the rollout.
3. Procedure
3.1 Freeze the release
Check out the release tag and confirm that it was signed by the release manager.
$ git fetch --tags origin $ git checkout release/2026.10.2 $ ./scripts/verify-signature.sh release/2026.10.2
3.2 Apply the configuration
Review the values below against the change ticket before applying them. The pool size must never exceed the connection limit agreed with the database team.
ledger: replicas: 4 database: pool _ size: 32 statement _ timeout _ ms: 5000 feature _ flags: async _ settlement: true
3.3 Roll out
Announce the start of the release in the operations channel.
Restart the deployment and follow its progress:
pods are replaced one at a time;
each new pod must pass its readiness check before the next one starts.
Stop and go to section 4 if any pod fails to become ready within five minutes.
kubectl -n ledger rollout restart deployment/ledger-api kubectl -n ledger rollout status deployment/ledger-api --timeout=10m

3.4 Verify
Run the query below fifteen minutes after the last pod has started. Every settlement created in that period should be in the SETTLED or PENDING state.
SELECT status, count(*) at > now() - interval '15 minutes'
FROM settlements WHERE created _ GROUP BY status;
After the rollout
Close the change ticket and record the release tag.
Post the verification query output in the ticket.
Hand the dashboards back to the on-call engineer.
4. Rollback
Roll back without waiting for approval when any threshold in the table is crossed.

SymptomThresholdActionError rate on /settleabove 2% for 5 minuteskubectl rollout undo, then page the duty managerSettlement latency (p99)above 1,500 msScale to 6 replicas; roll back if no change in 10 minutesDatabase connectionsabove 90% of the limitReduce pool _size to 24 and redeployPods not readyany pod after 5 minutesRoll back immediately
